summary.plain: A beam of neutrinos made at the J-PARC accelerator in Tokai, on Japan's Pacific coast, is aimed 295 km across the country at the Super-Kamiokande detector under a mountain near Kamioka. By comparing what arrives with what was sent, T2K found that muon neutrinos turn into electron neutrinos, and is now comparing neutrinos with antineutrinos.
summary.technical: Long-baseline accelerator neutrino oscillation experiment: a 30 GeV proton beam from the J-PARC main ring produces a narrow-band muon-(anti)neutrino beam, measured on-axis by INGRID and 2.5 degrees off-axis by ND280 at 280 m, then detected 295 km away at Super-Kamiokande. Data taking began January 2010; observed electron-neutrino appearance (evidence 2011, PRL 107 041801; observation 2014, PRL 112 061802) and reported a constraint on the CP-violating phase δCP (Nature 580, 339, 2020). Upgraded ND280 (Super-FGD, two high-angle TPCs, TOF) commissioned December 2023 alongside a beam-power record of 760 kW, beginning the T2K-II phase; Hyper-Kamiokande is its planned successor.

unique_capabilities.quote: T2K is the world's first off-axis neutrino experiment, with ND280 and Super K positioned 2.5 degrees away from the centre of the neutrino beam.
unique_capabilities.value: The world's first off-axis long-baseline neutrino experiment
